Latin word

dominor

dominor, dominārī, dominātus sum

verb, first conjugation, deponent; in + abl. or inter + acc.

be master, rule; of things, prevail, take over

In this lexicon

  • dominate

    the recommended word · classical · Verg. G. 1.154: sterilēs dominantur avēnae (Lewis & Short); Vulg. Prov. 16.32: quī dominātur animō suō

Examples

  • inter nitentia culta īnfēlīx lolium et sterilēs dominantur avēnae

    among the gleaming crops the wretched darnel and barren wild oats take overVerg. G. 1.153–154 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for dominate

  • Melior est patiēns virō fortī, et quī dominātur animō suō expugnātōre urbium.

    Better is the patient man than the strong, and he who rules his own spirit than one who takes cities.Vulg. Prov. 16.32

    In the entry for dominate
